item.title: Chinese foreign ministry slams Taiwan leader's separatist rhetoric
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Chinese foreign ministry slams Taiwan leader's separatist rhetoric BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland and Taiwan belong to one and the same China, and this constitutes the real status quo in the Taiwan Strait, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing after Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te sought to solicit external support for "Taiwan independence" in a speech in Taipei on Saturday. No matter what Lai says or does, it can't change the historical and legal fact that Taiwan belongs to China, nor can it alter the doomed failure of "Taiwan independence," still less can it stop the overwhelming trend that China will ultimately be reunified, she said. The so-called democracy touted by Lai cannot disguise his separatist agenda, she noted. Taiwan's return to China is an important part of the victorious outcomes of World War II and the post-war international order, the spokesperson said.

item.title: Mainland criticizes Taiwan's actions against fishing vessels near Dongsha Islands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Mainland criticizes Taiwan's actions against fishing vessels near Dongsha Islands On Wednesday, the Chinese mainland criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities for taking dangerous actions against mainland vessels after the island's coast guard authority claimed that they had "expelled two mainland fishing boats" from waters near the Dongsha Islands and used water cannons against one of the vessels. Chen Binhua, spokesman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press conference that China has "indisputable sovereignty" over the South China Sea islands, including the Dongsha Islands, and their surrounding waters. "Mainland vessels conducting operations in relevant waters are completely lawful and legitimate," Chen said, adding that the mainland will firmly safeguard the safety of people's lives and property. Taiwan's coast guard authority recently claimed that two mainland fishing vessels had entered waters near Dongsha and were "expelled in accordance with the law" on Oct 1. One of the vessels was forced to retreat after water cannons were used when it refused to weigh anchor, according to the authority. Chen criticized the DPP authorities for clinging to a "Taiwan independence" separatist position and using dangerous and violent methods to deal with mainland vessels, saying such actions endangered the lives and property of those involved. "Such actions deliberately fuel confrontation and antagonism across the Taiwan Strait," Chen said, warning that the DPP authorities "must bear all consequences arising from them".

item.title: Mainland imposes sanctions on companies tied to Taiwan separatists
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Mainland imposes sanctions on companies tied to Taiwan separatists The Chinese mainland respects and protects Taiwan compatriots' rights to freedom of speech and expression, while leaving no room for ambiguity on fundamental principles, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Chen Binhua, spokesman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to recent controversy over Taiwan entertainer Tsai Kang-yong, also known as Kevin Tsai, attending the inauguration ceremony of the campaign headquarters of Shen Pao-yang, the Democratic Progressive Party candidate for the Taipei mayoral election. Chen emphasized that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China and that the one-China principle remains the political foundation for cross-Strait relations. He said the actions of Shen, whom the mainland has labeled a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist, are widely known. "Any form of 'Taiwan independence' separatist activity constitutes a serious violation of the fundamental interests of the Chinese nation, and we firmly oppose all such activities," Chen said. Tsai, 64, has been active on both sides of the Taiwan Strait as a host and writer in recent years, participating in a number of mainland-based shows. Following his appearance at Shen's campaign event on Oct 4, several mainland companies announced that they would end their cooperation with Tsai and remove related content. Chen said the mainland respects and protects Taiwan compatriots' legitimate rights to freedom of speech and expression, but stressed that there can be no ambiguity on issues of principle. "No individual or force can seek to benefit from the mainland's development while at the same time colluding with 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces," Chen said, describing such individuals as "two-faced". Shen, founder of the Kuma Academy in Taiwan, has promoted separatist ideologies on the island. After being identified by the mainland as a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist, he was prohibited from entering the mainland, and organizations affiliated with him were restricted from cooperating with the mainland. A recent investigation found that Shen's father, Shen Tu-cheng, continued trade and business cooperation with relevant mainland enterprises under the name of a new company, VWAY, after his original company was sanctioned in June last year. Chen accused Shen of repeatedly advocating "anti-China" positions while obstructing cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, while at the same time working with relatives to seek profits from the mainland, calling such actions "disgraceful". "The mainland will not allow enterprises associated with diehard 'Taiwan independence' separatists to seek profits on the mainland," Chen said, adding that the mainland has decided to impose sanctions on VWAY and take necessary measures, including prohibiting the company from conducting any transactions or cooperation with mainland organizations, enterprises, and individuals.

item.title: Mainland denies Taiwan's claims of 'transnational suppression' in US surveillance case
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Mainland denies Taiwan's claims of 'transnational suppression' in US surveillance case The Chinese mainland on Wednesday rejected accusations from Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities of "transnational suppression" regarding the alleged surveillance of Lai Ching-te's son in the United States, describing them as groundless claims fabricated to provoke cross-Strait tensions for political gain. According to media reports, the US Federal Bureau of Investigation recently arrested a US woman who allegedly surveilled Lai's son in the US at the direction of the Chinese mainland. Chen Binhua, spokesman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said on Wednesday that he had no information about the matter. The DPP authorities described the case as "transnational suppression" and stated they were considering revisions to the so-called "anti-infiltration act" in response. Chen said the mainland firmly opposes the DPP authorities' collusion with external forces to make groundless accusations and spread falsehoods. He criticized the authorities for using "anti-China" rhetoric to fuel confrontation and provoke cross-Strait tensions for political gain. "Such sinister schemes and despicable practices cannot deceive Taiwan residents and will only be met with opposition and condemnation," Chen said.

item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi Launches National Defense Education Activity to Carry Forward the Long March Spirit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi Launches National Defense Education Activity to Carry Forward the Long March Spirit Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—Recently, the Taiwan Affairs Office of the CPC Jiangxi Provincial Committee organized all Party members and cadres of the office to visit the Jiangxi Provincial Museum for a national defense education activity. The group toured the exhibitions The Great Departure, the Eternal Long March: Exhibition on the History of the Central Red Army’s Departure for the Long March and Red Cradle: Exhibition of Jiangxi Revolutionary History. The activity aimed to guide cadres and staff in studying revolutionary traditions and enhancing their awareness of national defense. During the visit, the participants followed in the footsteps of history. They deeply reflected on the firm convictions and fearless sacrifice of revolutionary predecessors, as well as their arduous journey marked by perseverance and courage in overcoming hardships. The activity helped them gain a deep understanding of the paramount importance of national defense and national security, offering profound ideological refinement and spiritual edification. After the visit and study, Party members and cadres stated that the tour was both an in-depth education in revolutionary history and a vivid lesson in national defense. As cadres engaged in Taiwan-related work in the new era, they will inherit and carry forward the great Long March Spirit, uphold the glorious traditions and fine conduct of Communists, firmly embrace the holistic approach to national security, and continuously strengthen their awareness of national defense and potential risks. They will translate their insights into concrete actions to tackle challenges and deliver results. In line with their duties, they will deepen cross-strait exchanges and cooperation across various fields in Jiangxi. With high morale and pragmatic measures, they will promote high-quality development of Taiwan-related work in the province, actively foster spiritual affinity between compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, contribute to writing the Jiangxi chapter of Chinese modernization, and advance the great cause of national reunification.(Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Jiangxi) Related Stories

item.title: Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District, Kaifeng City Launches Taiwan-Related Publicity and Education Campaign in Enterprises
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—On October 10, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District, Kaifeng City, held an event to bring Taiwan-related publicity and education into enterprises. Representatives of local entrepreneurs gathered to study policies related to Taiwan affairs, discuss hot policy topics and ideas for industrial and commercial development, talk about cross-Strait integrated development, and express their patriotism and devotion to their home and country. During the event, the person in charge of the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yuwangtai District led participants in studying the overall strategy of the Communist Party of China (CPC) for resolving the Taiwan question in the new era. Drawing on the historical origins, cultural ties, and current developments across the Taiwan Strait, the official elaborated on the profound blood bond and shared destiny between compatriots on both sides of the Strait. The official also expounded on the core essence and spiritual connotations of the white paper The Taiwan Question and China’s Reunification in the New Era. The activity guided participants to accurately grasp the overall trend of cross-Strait relations and fully understand the historical and legal basis for Taiwan being an inalienable part of China’s territory. It also encouraged local entrepreneurs to actively explore practical ways to promote the message that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait are one family” in economic and trade exchanges and interactions, contributing to the deepening of cross-Strait integrated development. Representatives of enterprises at the event said that the activity served as a systematic study of policies and theories, a vivid lesson in patriotism and love for the homeland, and a heart-to-heart exchange that built consensus. Going forward, enterprises will draw on their actual operations and industrial strengths to actively identify entry points and areas of focus for linking their sectors with cross-Strait exchanges. They will proactively act as advocates and liaisons for cross-Strait exchanges, carry forward the kinship rooted in the shared origins of people across the Strait in daily business operations and external interactions, and build stronger momentum for cross-Strait integrated development. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Kaifeng)

item.title: 22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum to Be Held in Nanning, Guangxi, in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum to Be Held in Nanning, Guangxi, in October Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-13
Oct 13(Taiwan.cn)—In the golden autumn of Yongcheng (Nanning), Guangxi and Taiwan will write a new chapter in cooperation. The 22nd Guangxi-Taiwan Economic, Trade and Cultural Cooperation Forum is scheduled to take place in Nanning, Guangxi, from October 19 to 21, 2026. With the theme “Empowering a New Era through Digital Intelligence, Forging a Future via Guangxi-Taiwan Integrated Development,” the forum will be co-hosted by the People’s Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region and the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council. The forum will be held at a time when the Pinglu Canal has been officially completed and opened to navigation, and a series of events commemorating the 160th anniversary of Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s birth are underway. The full opening of the Pinglu Canal has turned the century-old vision of river-sea transportation laid out in Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s The International Development of China—connecting rivers to the sea and enabling integrated river-ocean shipping—from a blueprint into reality. Currently, Guangxi is accelerating the development of ten modern pillar industries. Following a path of digitalization, green development, and integration, it is leveraging artificial intelligence as a core driver to advance industrial transformation and upgrading. Meanwhile, Guangxi has rolled out systematic measures for its marine economy, ushering in a new phase of building strength through marine development and pursuing opening-up and growth. These development opportunities not only open up broad new space for Guangxi’s high-quality development but also inject strong momentum into exchanges and cooperation between Guangxi and Taiwan. The forum will feature an opening plenary session and two parallel thematic sub-forums: “Development Paths and Practices of Artificial Intelligence in Guangxi and Taiwan” and “Building a New Ecosystem for the Guangxi-Taiwan Marine Economy through River-Sea Coordination.” Taking digital and intelligent industries as the link and the Pinglu Canal as an open platform, participants from Guangxi and Taiwan will conduct in-depth exchanges and discussions on key areas of cooperation, including electronic information technology, artificial intelligence, port logistics, and marine fisheries, jointly exploring new paths for mutually beneficial cooperation. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi) Related Stories

item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.

item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps
item.description:
Published: 2026-01-29
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-01-29
BEIJING, Jan. 28 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for hyping up the so-called information security risks of applications from the mainland. Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated at a press conference that the DPP moves have deprived people in Taiwan, especially the youth, of their right to know and the freedom to use social networking platforms. Noting that such moves reveal the fear and insecurity of the DPP authorities, Zhang said they will have to face the dire consequences of their wayward actions.
